D1 research authoring, batch 87 (2026-09-27): three ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1-3 (scoliosis, chronic-kidney-disease, depressive-disorder) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. Rank order is EVIDENCE-LED: the scoliosis edge is first because its anchor supplies a prevalence near one in two in the largest cohort located, the renal edge is second because its anchors supply both a rate of decline and the anatomical substrate, and the mood edge is third because its largest rate comes from a self-selected volunteer sample.

DIRECTION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE SCOLIOSIS EDGE: the located reading is a SHARED DEVELOPMENTAL FIELD DEFECT rather than consequence, and the second anchor SELECTED ITS POPULATION ON CONGENITAL SCOLIOSIS and then reported dysraphism on MRI, so it measures the relationship in the opposite direction. The two anchors are therefore not convergent evidence and are not to be counted as such.

MEASUREMENT-CAVEAT GUARD, APPLIED TO THE RENAL EDGE: no validated spina bifida-specific eGFR formula exists, the proportion of adults at CKD stage 2 or higher ranged from 9.2 to 30.5 percent BY FORMULA ALONE, and up to 26.8 percent of adults were reclassified by a change of formula alone. Any stage or rate imported from this edge must name its formula, and the finding is registered for ADULTS because the four paediatric formulas disagree in direction as well as magnitude.

DIRECTION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE MOOD EDGE: none of the three anchors orders disability and mood in time. The strongest design, a propensity-matched administrative database study, measures CODED DIAGNOSES rather than current symptoms, and the largest rate, 48 percent, comes from a self-selected volunteer sample. No magnitude is presented as this identity's prevalence.

NO MAGNITUDE IS STATED FOR ANY EDGE AS A COMPLICATION RATE. The renal edge reports a rate of decline and a structural finding but NO TERMINAL OUTCOME, and no located anchor reports end-stage disease, dialysis or transplantation.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Scoliosis is the most frequently documented musculoskeletal accompaniment of spina bifida in the located adult literature, and the located cohort reports a prevalence close to one in two. A cross-sectional study of 580 adults attending a first consultation at a French multidisciplinary spina bifida referral centre, of whom 331 met the inclusion criteria with 221 open and 110 closed spina bifida, found that 176, 53 PERCENT, HAD SCOLIOSIS, 57 percent in the open and 45 percent in the closed form; compared with adults without scoliosis, those with scoliosis more frequently had open spina bifida (p EQUALS 0.03), a MORE CRANIALLY LOCATED lesion (p LESS THAN 0.0001), MORE SEVERE NEUROLOGICAL DEFICITS (p LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO 0.02) and POORER WALKING ABILITY with a mean Functional Ambulation Classification score of 3.5 against 6.1 (p LESS THAN 0.0001), while the odds of scoliosis were associated with an asymmetrical motor level and a Functional Ambulation Classification score below 4 (PMID 35717001). The same cohort reports that 69 PERCENT had chronic back pain, with NO DIFFERENCE in frequency between those with and without scoliosis, a null that is recorded on this edge because it is what stops back pain from being attributed to the deformity (PMID 35717001). A separate retrospective series of 247 children presenting with CONGENITAL scoliosis or kyphosis at a single Indian centre found ABNORMAL MRI FINDINGS consistent with occult spinal dysraphism in 130 of 229 congenital scoliosis cases, 53.7 PERCENT, with the highest incidence in failure-of-segmentation deformities at 66.6 percent and in mixed deformities at 65 percent, and diastematomyelia followed by tethered cord the most common anomalies (PMID 38581468). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the second anchor SELECTED ITS POPULATION ON SCOLIOSIS and therefore runs the relationship backwards, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THIS EDGE IS A CO-OCCURRENCE RATHER THAN A CONSEQUENCE, which is the located reading: the spinal dysraphism, the vertebral segmentation failure and the muscle imbalance that produces a deformity are all consequences of the same developmental field defect, so scoliosis in this population is recorded as a frequently accompanying deformity rather than as a secondary condition produced by the neural tube defect. The first anchor is a FIRST-CONSULTATION cohort at a single national referral centre, so its 53 percent is a referral-clinic prevalence and not a community prevalence, and its inclusion criterion of attending a first consultation at all is itself a selection effect. The second anchor is SELECTED ON CONGENITAL SCOLIOSIS AND KYPHOSIS and then reports occult dysraphism on MRI, so it is a REVERSE-SELECTION ANCHOR that quantifies how often a dysraphism is found when a deformity is the presenting problem, not how often a deformity is found when a dysraphism is the presenting problem; its 53.7 percent must not be transferred to the first anchor's population. The recorded null matters: 69 percent reported chronic back pain with NO DIFFERENCE between those with and without scoliosis, so an individual with back pain in this population must not have that pain attributed to the deformity on the strength of this edge. Individual claims require a dated spina bifida diagnosis with the OPEN OR CLOSED FORM and the ANATOMICAL LEVEL recorded, a Cobb angle with its measurement date and whether it is congenital or acquired, a neurological level and a Functional Ambulation Classification score, an MRI report, and a clinical determination separating a congenital dysraphism-associated deformity from a progressive neuromuscular one, from post-operative or post-immobilisation deformity, and from scoliosis arising after a shunt or other neurosurgical intervention.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared developmental-field mechanism operating through load asymmetry: the same failure of midline vertebral formation that leaves a dysraphic defect also produces wedge vertebrae, hemivertebrae and segmentation failures in the same vertebral bodies, so the spine is structurally asymmetric from birth, and because the muscles supplying the lower limbs and trunk are themselves affected by the neural defect, an already asymmetric column is loaded by an asymmetric musculature, which drives progressive lateral curvature through growth; the vector is named as the shared vertebral-and-neuromuscular asymmetry rather than as a mechanical consequence of the open defect's closure, because the located anchors report a congenital-segmentation mechanism and neither attributes curvature to the defect's repair.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at large-cross-sectional-cohort and reverse-selection-retrospective-paediatric-series class, following the file's existing neurological, musculoskeletal and congenital pathway scope. The French cohort is the anchor that supplies the prevalence and the severity gradient, 53 percent of 331 adults with 57 percent in open and 45 percent in closed forms and a stepwise rise with more cranially located lesions, more severe neurological deficit and poorer walking ability, which is what makes the anatomical-level guard necessary rather than optional (PMID 35717001). The Indian series is registered for a structurally different reason, namely that it quantifies the reverse direction, occult dysraphism found on MRI in 53.7 percent of a congenital-scoliosis population, and it is retained precisely so that the two anchors are not counted as convergent when they in fact measure opposite directions (PMID 38581468). The chronic-back-pain null from the first anchor is carried on the face of the edge because it is the located reason the deformity cannot be used to explain pain in this population. Because the two anchors measure different directions in different populations and neither establishes that the deformity causes any complication, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states no complication rate for the deformity itself.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THIS EDGE IS A CO-OCCURRENCE AND NOT A CONSEQUENCE: the located reading is that spinal dysraphism, vertebral segmentation failure and the deformity share one developmental field defect, and no located anchor establishes that the neural tube defect produces the curvature causally (PMID 35717001, PMID 38581468). THE SECOND ANCHOR IS A REVERSE-SELECTION ANCHOR: it selected its population on CONGENITAL SCOLIOSIS AND KYPHOSIS and then reported occult dysraphism on MRI, so its 53.7 percent measures how often a dysraphism is found WHEN A DEFORMITY IS THE PRESENTING PROBLEM and CANNOT BE TRANSFERRED to the first anchor's spina bifida-selected population (PMID 38581468). THE FIRST ANCHOR IS A FIRST-CONSULTATION COHORT AT A SINGLE NATIONAL REFERRAL CENTRE, so its 53 percent is a REFERRAL-CLINIC PREVALENCE and not a community prevalence, and attending a first consultation is itself a selection effect; only 331 of 580 screened adults met the inclusion criteria (PMID 35717001). A CONTRADICTORY NULL IS CARRIED: 69 PERCENT of the same cohort reported chronic back pain with NO STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE between those with and without scoliosis, so pain in this population must not be attributed to the deformity on the strength of this edge (PMID 35717001). THE ANCHORS DISAGREE ON THE OPEN-CLOSED GRADIENT IN A WAY THE EDGE CANNOT RESOLVE, the first reporting 57 percent versus 45 percent for open versus closed forms while the second reports a 53.7 percent MRI abnormality rate in a deformity-selected population that is not stratified by form at all. NO located anchor reports how scoliosis progresses, whether it worsens with age, at what Cobb angle surgery is indicated, or what proportion of affected adults require operative correction, and none separates a congenital dysraphism-associated curve from an acquired or iatrogenic one.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: A congenital or progressive neuromuscular curve arising from the same defect by a different route, including a post-operative or post-immobilisation deformity and a curve developing after shunt insertion or other neurosurgical intervention
A fracture or vertebral malformation producing secondary deformity in an already abnormal column, which would give a wholly different mechanism and a different management pathway

Pain arising from tethered cord, disc disease, hip pathology or urological causes rather than from the curve itself, which the located cohort's back-pain null makes mandatory to consider before attributing pain to scoliosis
An idiopathic adolescent curve coinciding with, but unconnected to, a dysraphism found on MRI, which the reverse-selection anchor's design cannot exclude
Post-operative or hardware-related deformity after spinal fusion for a dysraphism or for hydrocephalus shunting, which is common in this population and is not modelled in any located anchor

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Renal deterioration is the recognised long-term consequence of the neurogenic bladder that accompanies this identity, and the located evidence both quantifies the decline and documents the upper-tract damage that precedes it. A cross-sectional study of 209 children with a median age of 10.3 years and 164 adults with a median age of 26.3 years found that eGFR DECREASED FOR EVERY ADULT FORMULA EVALUATED, in the range -1.3 to -2.2 ml/min/1.73 m2 per year, which the authors describe as GREATER THAN TWICE THE GENERAL POPULATION RATE, in the first three decades after age 18, while in children eGFR decreased by -0.7 to -1.8, remained stable or even increased depending on the formula used; the PROPORTION OF ADULTS WITH CKD STAGE 2 OR HIGHER VARIED FROM 9.2 TO 30.5 PERCENT DEPENDING ON THE FORMULA, and comparing any two formulas assigned 8.5 to 26.8 percent of adults a DIFFERENT CKD STAGE (PMID 31956092). A retrospective review of 117 children with neuropathic bladder at a single centre, mean age 6.7 years, in whom the LEADING CAUSE OF NEUROPATHIC BLADDER WAS NEUROSPINAL DYSRAPHISM IN 103 CASES, 88.1 PERCENT, found hydronephrosis in 44 patients, 35.9 PERCENT, parenchymal thinning in 20, 17.1 percent, increased parenchymal echo in 20, 17.1 percent, and bladder trabeculation or wall thickening in 51, 43.6 percent (PMID 36999336). The same paper frames the causal sequence explicitly, neurogenic detrusor overactivity contributing to detrusor-sphincter dysfunction and to incontinence, with UPPER URINARY TRACT DETERIORATION named as the progressive and insidious at the same time preventable result of neuropathic bladder, and states that despite worldwide neural tube defect prevention strategies patients will continue to be born with a neuropathic bladder at risk of long-term renal damage (PMID 36999336). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that no located anchor reports a cumulative incidence of end-stage disease, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF IS UNSTABLE, which is the located finding and is stated first: no validated spina bifida-specific eGFR formula exists, the proportion of adults classified as CKD stage 2 or higher ranged from 9.2 to 30.5 PERCENT BY FORMULA ALONE, and comparing any two formulas assigned 8.5 to 26.8 percent of adults a different stage, so a claim cannot import a stage or a rate without naming the formula and acknowledging that a different formula would have produced a different answer for up to a quarter of the cohort. The first anchor is CROSS-SECTIONAL, so it characterises a rate of decline between age strata rather than following any individual longitudinally, and its authors state plainly that they CANNOT RELIABLY DETERMINE WHETHER eGFR CHANGED DURING CHILDHOOD because the four paediatric formulas disagree in direction as well as magnitude, one showing a fall, one stability and one a rise. The second anchor is a SINGLE-CENTRE PAEDIATRIC UROLOGY COHORT in which neuropathic bladder was the inclusion criterion rather than this identity, so although 88.1 percent had a neuro-spinal dysraphism aetiology the imaging findings are upper-tract findings in a bladder population and not renal outcomes in a spina bifida population. NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE, DIALYSIS OR TRANSPLANTATION as an outcome, so this edge carries a decline and a structural-damage finding and no terminal outcome. Individual claims require a dated spina bifida diagnosis with neurological level recorded, a named eGFR or creatinine-cystatin C formula with the assay platform, serial renal function with the measurement interval, a documented upper-tract imaging history including ultrasound, voiding cystography and where relevant nuclear renography, a documented urological management history including intermittent catheterisation and any anticholinergic or intravesical therapy, and a clinical determination separating neurogenic upper-tract damage from obstructive uropathy, from recurrent infection alone, from stone disease and from any independent renal disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is sustained high bladder pressure transmitted to the upper tract: neurogenic detrusor overactivity from the spinal defect, combined with detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia in which the sphincter contracts against a contracting detrusor, generates bladder pressures above the ureteral drainage threshold, and those repeated pressure waves are transmitted up the ureters to the renal pelvis, so the papillae are exposed to a pressure load they cannot buffer, which produces reflux and hydronephrosis, which produces parenchymal thinning, which produces a falling filtration rate; the vector is named as the pressure-and-stasis cascade rather than as reflux alone or as infection alone, because the located anchor reports hydronephrosis, parenchymal thinning and bladder trabeculation together and describes the aim of management as reducing bladder pressure and minimising urine stasis to PREVENT OR AT LEAST ATTENUATE renal disease.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cross-sectional-cohort-with-multiple-eGFR-formulas and retrospective-paediatric-urology-cohort class, following the file's existing renal, urological and neurological pathway scope. The eGFR study is the anchor that supplies the rate of decline and, more importantly, the measurement instability, and its conclusion that the observed adult decline is greater than twice the general population rate is registered together with the authors' own statement that they cannot reliably determine whether eGFR changed during childhood, because reporting only the decline would overstate the certainty of the finding (PMID 31956092). The neuropathic-bladder cohort is registered because it is the located source that documents the anatomical substrate of the decline, hydronephrosis in 35.9 percent and parenchymal thinning in 17.1 percent in a population whose leading aetiology was neuro-spinal dysraphism at 88.1 percent, and because it names upper urinary tract deterioration as the preventable end of the pathway, which is what converts a descriptive association into a clinically actionable one (PMID 36999336). Because the located evidence describes a rate of decline and a structural finding but no terminal outcome, and because the measurement is formula-dependent, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and refuses to state a single stage or a single prevalence.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THE MEASUREMENT IS UNSTABLE AND NO VALIDATED SPINA BIFIDA-SPECIFIC eGFR FORMULA EXISTS: the proportion of adults classified as CKD STAGE 2 OR HIGHER RANGED FROM 9.2 TO 30.5 PERCENT BY FORMULA ALONE, and comparing any two formulas assigned 8.5 TO 26.8 PERCENT of adults a DIFFERENT CKD STAGE, so any stage or rate imported from this edge must name its formula and acknowledge that another formula would have reclassified up to a quarter of the cohort (PMID 31956092). THE FOUR PAEDIATRIC FORMULAS DISAGREE IN DIRECTION AS WELL AS MAGNITUDE, with eGFR falling by -0.7 to -1.8 in two, remaining stable in one and RISING BY +2.7 PER YEAR in another, and the authors state they CANNOT RELIABLY DETERMINE WHETHER eGFR CHANGED DURING CHILDHOOD; the finding therefore applies to adults and is not extrapolated to the paediatric population (PMID 31956092). THE FIRST ANCHOR IS CROSS-SECTIONAL and characterises a rate of decline between age strata rather than following any individual longitudinally, and it also notes that spina bifida carries variable muscle mass which itself distorts creatinine-based estimation (PMID 31956092). THE SECOND ANCHOR'S INCLUSION CRITERION WAS NEUROPATHIC BLADDER, NOT THIS IDENTITY, and although 88.1 percent of its 117 children had a neuro-spinal dysraphism aetiology, its imaging findings are UPPER-TRACT FINDINGS IN A BLADDER POPULATION and not renal outcomes in a spina bifida population (PMID 36999336). NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS END-STAGE RENAL DISEASE, DIALYSIS OR TRANSPLANTATION as an outcome, so this edge carries a decline and a structural-damage finding and NO TERMINAL OUTCOME. NO located anchor separates neurogenic upper-tract damage from obstructive uropathy, from stone disease, from recurrent infection acting alone, or from an independent pre-existing renal disease, and none reports whether active urological management alters the decline.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Obstructive uropathy from stones, from ureteric stents or from any anatomical obstruction, which produces hydronephrosis by a mechanical route indistinguishable on ultrasound
Recurrent febrile urinary tract infection acting on its own, which is common in this population and which the located anchors do not separate from pressure-mediated damage
Any independent pre-existing renal disease or a renal malformation associated with the same developmental field defect, which the located anchors do not exclude

Distraction of muscle mass reducing creatinine-based estimation, which the first anchor names explicitly as a source of error in this population and which is a MEASUREMENT artefact rather than a renal outcome
Prior urological instrumentation, including repeated cystoscopy, ureteric stenting and augmentation cystoplasty, each of which has its own renal and upper-tract consequences

sourceReferences.note: RETROSPECTIVE REVIEW OF 117 CHILDREN WITH NEUROPATHIC BLADDER followed for at least one year in combined paediatric urology and nephrology units, 73 female and 44 male, mean age 6.7 years, patients under one year excluded. THE LEADING CAUSE OF NEUROPATHIC BLADDER WAS NEUROSPINAL DYSRAPHISM WITH 103 OF 117 PATIENTS, 88.1 PERCENT. Urinary tract ultrasound revealed HYDRONEPHROSIS IN 44 PATIENTS, 35.9 PERCENT, PARENCHYMAL THINNING IN 20, 17.1 PERCENT, increased parenchymal echo in 20, 17.1 PERCENT, and BLADDER TRABECULATION OR INCREASED WALL THICKNESS IN 51, 43.6 PERCENT. The authors state that neurogenic detrusor overactivity contributes to detrusor-sphincter dysfunction producing lower urinary tract symptoms such as incontinence, that UPPER URINARY TRACT DETERIORATION is among the most progressive and at the same time preventable results of neuropathic bladder, that the aim is reduction in bladder pressures and minimisation of urine stasis in order to prevent or at least attenuate renal disease, and that despite worldwide neural tube defect prevention strategies patients will continue to be born with a neuropathic bladder at risk of long-term renal damage. Registered for the anatomical substrate of the decline and for the pathway framing.

sourceReferences.note: Narrative review addressing the progression of paediatric lower urinary tract dysfunction to kidney disease in adolescents and the case for precision medicine in treatment. The authors frame the same pathway this edge describes, that a neurogenic bladder in a child with a spinal defect produces sustained detrusor pressure which is transmitted to the upper tract, and that bladder pressure reduction and reduction of urinary stasis are the levers by which renal damage is prevented or attenuated. Registered as a third source because it is the located review that names the adolescent transition as the point at which paediatric lower urinary tract dysfunction progresses to kidney disease, which is the temporal claim the two cohort anchors do not themselves make. DISCLOSED: a NARRATIVE REVIEW rather than a cohort, contributing the trajectory and the therapeutic rationale rather than a rate, so it cannot supply a magnitude for this identity.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: World J Nephrol. 2021;10(4):37-46. Review of paediatric lower urinary tract dysfunction progressing to kidney disease in adolescents, and the case for precision medicine in treatment, framing bladder pressure and urinary stasis reduction as the levers preventing renal damage.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Psychological distress is the most consistently reported comorbidity of this identity in the located literature, and three independent designs agree on its magnitude. A cross-sectional survey of around 195 adults with congenital urologic conditions recruited to include adults with spina bifida, using the Neurogenic Bladder Symptom Score and Patient-Reported Outcome Measures Information System instruments, found RATES OF DEPRESSION, ANXIETY AND SOCIAL ISOLATION OF 48 PERCENT, 47 PERCENT AND 43 PERCENT RESPECTIVELY, with COMORBID DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY IN 39 PERCENT, and on adjusted regression analysis LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION WAS ASSOCIATED WITH DEPRESSION (p LESS THAN .001), with anxiety (p LESS THAN .001), with the composite depression-anxiety score (p LESS THAN .001) and with social isolation (p EQUALS .010) (PMID 33221413). A large federated-database study of 18- to 25-year-olds using TriNetX, in which PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHING IDENTIFIED 1,494 PATIENTS IN EACH COHORT, found that spina bifida patients were more likely to have DEPRESSION (odds ratio 1.949, 95% CI 1.64 to 2.317) and ANXIETY (1.603, 95% CI 1.359 to 1.891) than matched patients without spina bifida, and also more likely to have SOMATOFORM DISORDERS (2.102, 95% CI 1.052 to 4.199) and SUICIDAL IDEATIONS OR ATTEMPTS AND SELF-HARM (1.424, 95% CI 1.014 to 1.999) (PMID 36933266). A Norwegian cross-sectional study of 30 persons with spina bifida aged 50 and over, mean age 57.5, found 30 PERCENT scored above the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale anxiety threshold and 20 PERCENT above the depression threshold, IN THE SAME RANGE AS PREVIOUS STUDIES of spina bifida but HIGHER THAN PERSONS WITH CHRONIC SPINAL CORD INJURY AND NORMS, with the depression score correlating with pain and fatigue scores (PMID 34826231). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the age range spans three very different populations, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED, because all three anchors are cross-sectional or database-derived and none can order the disability and the mood in time. The first anchor is a VOLUNTEER SURVEY DISTRIBUTED VIA FACEBOOK ADVERTISING to individuals with congenital urologic conditions, so its 48 percent is a self-selected respondent rate and not a population prevalence, and its own authors frame the finding as identifying CHARACTERISTICS ASSOCIATED WITH rather than as establishing consequence. The second anchor is the strongest design in the batch because PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHING addresses confounding by indication and by care-seeking, but it is an ADMINISTRATIVE-CODE study in which depression is an ICD-10-coded diagnosis rather than an instrument score, so it captures treated or recorded depression rather than current symptoms, and it reports a matched ORDERS RATIO rather than a prevalence. The third anchor is a THIRTY-PARTICIPANT SAMPLE in the oldest age band studied, with 18 women and 12 men, of whom 26 had myelomeningocele and six hydrocephalus, so it cannot be read as a rate for the whole adult population. A substantive finding runs across the anchors and is recorded rather than smoothed: the third anchor reports symptoms HIGHER THAN PERSONS WITH CHRONIC SPINAL CORD INJURY, and the second reports HIGHER rates of depressive and anxiety disorders than matched peers, so this is not a generic consequence of chronic disability. Individual claims require a dated spina bifida diagnosis with neurological level and mobility status recorded, a structured depression instrument administered and scored with the instrument and its threshold named, an explicit timeline establishing whether mood symptoms predate or follow the onset of the condition and of any surgical complication, an assessment of pain, fatigue and sleep as competing or mediating variables, and a clinical determination separating depressive disorder from adjustment disorder to disability, from grief, from medication effects and from any neurocognitive impairment inherent to the condition.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a self-reinforcing loop in which the physical burden of the condition sustains the distress and the distress in turn degrades the self-management the condition requires: continence failure produces urgency, urgency produces avoidance of public and occupational settings, avoidance produces social isolation and reduced activity, reduced activity worsens the fatigue and pain that the first anchor identifies as correlating with the depression score, and the fatigue in turn reduces the motivation and executive capacity needed for the intermittent catheterisation and mobility regime on which renal and skin protection depend; the vector is named as this behavioural-and-burden loop rather than as a shared neural substrate, because the strongest anchor in the set identifies a lower urinary tract symptom score as the independent correlate of depression, and because the second anchor shows the excess over matched peers is specific to this population rather than to disability in general.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at volunteer-survey-with-adjusted-regression, propensity-matched-administrative-database-cohort and small-cross-sectional-instrument-study class, following the file's existing neurological, urological and psychological pathway scope. The database cohort is the anchor that carries the edge because propensity score matching is the only located design that addresses confounding, and it supplies both a magnitude and a specificity claim, an adjusted odds ratio of 1.949 for depression alongside elevated rates of somatoform disorder and of suicidal ideation or attempts and self-harm, which are findings that would be irresponsible to omit from a mood edge in this population (PMID 36933266). The volunteer survey is registered because it is the anchor that identifies LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION as the independent correlate of depression, anxiety, the composite score and social isolation, which is what makes the mechanism claim a clinical one rather than a generic disability claim, and its 48 percent and 47 percent prevalences are disclosed as self-selected (PMID 33221413). The Norwegian cohort is registered for the comparison its authors make against persons with chronic spinal cord injury and against norms, which is the located evidence that the excess is not generic, and its thirty-participant sample is disclosed (PMID 34826231). Because the three anchors span ages 18 to 25, working age and 50 and over, and because none orders disability and mood in time, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states no population rate.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: THE FIRST ANCHOR IS A SELF-SELECTED VOLUNTEER SAMPLE: the survey was distributed via FACEBOOK ADVERTISING to individuals with congenital urologic conditions and around 195 participated, so its 48 percent depression, 47 percent anxiety and 43 percent social isolation rates are RESPONDENT RATES and not population prevalences (PMID 33221413). DIRECTION IS UNRESOLVED: all three anchors are cross-sectional or database-derived and none can order the disability and the mood in time, and the first anchor's own framing is that it identifies CHARACTERISTICS ASSOCIATED WITH the outcomes (PMID 33221413, PMID 36933266, PMID 34826231). THE SECOND ANCHOR MEASURES ICD-10-CODED DIAGNOSES rather than instrument scores, so it captures TREATED OR RECORDED DEPRESSION rather than current symptoms, and it reports a MATCHED ORDERS RATIO rather than a prevalence (PMID 36933266). THE THIRD ANCHOR HAS THIRTY PARTICIPANTS in the oldest age band studied, 18 women and 12 men, of whom 26 had myelomeningocele and six hydrocephalus, so it cannot be read as a rate for the whole adult population and its 20 percent above-threshold figure is small-numerated (PMID 34826231). THE THREE ANCHORS SPAN THREE VERY DIFFERENT AGE BANDS, 18 to 25, working age, and 50 and over, and no located anchor reports a longitudinal course, so a rate from one age band cannot be transferred to another. NO located anchor reports whether treating the depression changes continence, mobility, renal outcome or wound integrity, nor the reverse; the first anchor's finding that pain and fatigue correlate with the depression score identifies mediating variables that no located anchor partitions from one another.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Adjustment disorder to disability, which is a different diagnosis with a different course and which the located anchors do not separate, particularly in the age band where onset and adjustment coincide

Pain and fatigue, which the third anchor reports as correlating with the depression score and which are therefore plausible mediators rather than confounders, and which the located evidence does not partition
Neurocognitive impairment inherent to the condition, whose association with the second anchor's cognitive disengagement findings and with mood could not be separated in any located anchor
Repeated neurosurgical and urological intervention, whose own psychological burden is unmeasured in every located anchor and which would supply an alternative route to distress
Social isolation as a cause rather than a consequence, since the first anchor reports social isolation at 43 percent and its cross-sectional design cannot order it against depression

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because psychological distress is the most consistently reported comorbidity of this identity, with three anchors in three different age bands and two different designs, one of them propensity-matched, and because the target identity, depressive-disorder, is the most heavily targeted identity in the registry at 94 incoming edges while this catalog identity had ZERO. The conservative framing is explicit that the largest of the three rates comes from a self-selected volunteer sample, that the design that controls for confounding measures coded diagnoses rather than symptoms, and that direction is unresolved.

sourceReferences.citation: Showen A, Copp HL, Allen IE, et al. Characteristics Associated With Depression, Anxiety, and Social Isolation in Adults With Spina Bifida. Urology. 2021 Mar;149:255-262. doi: 10.1016/j.urology.2020.11.016. PMID 33221413.
sourceReferences.note: ANONYMOUS SURVEY of around 195 adults with congenital urologic conditions recruited via FACEBOOK ADVERTISING, with adults with spina bifida included, assessing lower urinary tract dysfunction with the NEUROGENIC BLADDER SYMPTOM SCORE and depression, anxiety and social isolation with PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOME MEASURES INFORMATION SYSTEM instruments, and constructing a composite depression-anxiety score. RATES OF DEPRESSION, ANXIETY AND SOCIAL ISOLATION WERE 48 PERCENT, 47 PERCENT AND 43 PERCENT RESPECTIVELY, with COMORBID DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY IN 39 PERCENT of subjects. On ADJUSTED REGRESSION, LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION WAS ASSOCIATED WITH DEPRESSION (p LESS THAN .001), ANXIETY (p LESS THAN .001), the composite depression-anxiety score (p LESS THAN .001) and SOCIAL ISOLATION (p EQUALS .010). The authors conclude that depression, anxiety and social isolation are common in individuals with spina bifida relative to the general population and associated with lower urinary tract dysfunction, and recommend interventions targeting lower urinary tract symptoms and function, group psychotherapy, and comorbid depression and anxiety. Registered as the anchor that identifies a lower urinary tract symptom score as the INDEPENDENT CORRELATE, which is what makes the mechanism claim clinical rather than generic. DISCLOSED: a SELF-SELECTED VOLUNTEER SAMPLE, so the percentages are respondent rates, and the authors' own wording is that characteristics are ASSOCIATED WITH the outcomes.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Urology. 2021;149(3):255-262. Volunteer survey of approximately 195 adults with spina bifida: depression 48 percent, anxiety 47 percent, social isolation 43 percent and comorbid depression with anxiety 39 percent, with lower urinary tract dysfunction independently associated with depression, anxiety, the composite score and social isolation on adjusted regression.

sourceReferences.citation: Sciscent BY, Hallan DR, Rizk EB. Mental health and substance use disorders in young adults with spina bifida. J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2023 Mar 17:1-7. doi: 10.3171/2023.2.PEDS22504. PMID 36933266.
sourceReferences.note: RETROSPECTIVE TRINETX QUERY IDENTIFYING 18- TO 25-YEAR-OLD PATIENTS WITH SPINA BIFIDA, COMPARED AFTER PROPENSITY SCORE MATCHING WITH 1,494 PATIENTS IN EACH COHORT, and additionally compared with patients with a spinal cord injury, with subgroup analysis for hydrocephalus and neurogenic bladder. AFTER MATCHING, SPINA BIFIDA PATIENTS WERE MORE LIKELY THAN MATCHED PEERS TO HAVE DEPRESSION (odds ratio 1.949, 95% CI 1.64 TO 2.317), ANXIETY (1.603, 95% CI 1.359 TO 1.891), SOMATOFORM DISORDERS (2.102, 95% CI 1.052 TO 4.199) and SUICIDAL IDEATIONS OR ATTEMPTS AND SELF-HARM (1.424, 95% CI 1.014 TO 1.999); the prevalence of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and eating disorders was comparable between cohorts. Patients also had increased rates of nicotine dependence (1.546, 95% CI 1.22 to 1.959) but not of alcohol or opioid disorders, and the presence of hydrocephalus and neurogenic bladder WAS NOT ASSOCIATED with significantly increased rates of any measured disorder, a null recorded on this edge. Compared with spinal cord injury, spina bifida patients were more likely to have anxiety (1.377, 95% CI 1.028 to 1.845) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (1.875, 95% CI 1.084 to 3.242) but had LOWER nicotine dependence (0.682, 95% CI 0.482 to 0.963) and opioid-related disorders (0.434, 95% CI 0.223 to 0.845). Registered as the anchor that carries the edge, being the only design that addresses confounding. DISCLOSED: ICD-10-CODED DIAGNOSES rather than instrument scores, so TREATED OR RECORDED DEPRESSION rather than current symptoms, and a matched odds ratio rather than a prevalence.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2023. Propensity-matched TriNetX study of 1,494 patients aged 18 to 25 with spina bifida versus 1,494 matched controls: depression odds ratio 1.949, anxiety 1.603, somatoform disorder 2.102 and suicidal ideation or attempts and self-harm 1.424; hydrocephalus and neurogenic bladder were not associated with increased rates of any measured disorder.

sourceReferences.citation: Lidal IB, Lundberg Larsen K. Anxiety, depression, and fatigue in middle-aged and older persons with spina bifida: a cross-sectional study. Disabil Rehabil. 2022 Dec;44(25):7936-7946. doi: 10.1080/09638288.2021.2003453. PMID 34826231.
sourceReferences.note: CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY OF 30 PERSONS WITH SPINA BIFIDA AGED 50 AND OVER LIVING IN NORWAY, 18 women and 12 men, mean age 57.5 years, of whom 26 had MYELOMENINGOCELE and six had HYDROCEPHALUS, assessed with the HOSPITAL ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION SCALE and the Fatigue Severity Scale. THIRTY PERCENT scored above the HADS anxiety threshold and TWENTY PERCENT above the HADS depression threshold, which the authors state is IN THE SAME RANGE AS PREVIOUS STUDIES of spina bifida but HIGHER COMPARED WITH PERSONS WITH CHRONIC SPINAL CORD INJURY AND NORMS. The HADS depression score CORRELATED WITH PAIN AND FATIGUE SCORES, and 40 PERCENT reported fatigue symptoms. The authors conclude that symptoms of anxiety and depression were more common than among persons with chronic spinal cord injury and population norms, recommend screening for psychological distress and fatigue at follow-up and rehabilitation visits, suggest that interventions to reduce pain may influence distress or fatigue, and advise enquiry into medication effects on fatigue with a thorough medication review. Registered for the comparison against persons with chronic spinal cord injury, which is the located evidence that the excess is not generic disability. DISCLOSED: A THIRTY-PARTICIPANT SAMPLE IN THE OLDEST AGE BAND STUDIED, so the 20 percent above-threshold figure is small-numerated and cannot be read as a rate for the adult population.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Disabil Rehabil. 2022;44(8):7936-7946. Cross-sectional study of 30 Norwegian adults aged 50 and over with spina bifida: 30 percent above the HADS anxiety threshold and 20 percent above the depression threshold, higher than persons with chronic spinal cord injury and population norms; depression score correlated with pain and fatigue, and 40 percent reported fatigue symptoms.

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 87: no alias duplication found. The catalog carries hydrocephalus, scoliosis, charcot-arthropathy, syringomyelia and lumbar-spinal-stenosis as separate identities; the only alias is the literal 'spina bifida residuals', which names the same condition and is not a duplicate.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 87: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so all three edges are new. Targets scoliosis and charcot-arthropathy had 2 and 1 registered incoming edges respectively, while depressive-disorder at 94 is the most heavily targeted identity in the registry.

A REVERSAL OF SIBLING PRIORITY IS RECORDED: hydrocephalus is the condition most often named in the same breath as this identity, and the catalog already carries a hydrocephalus identity with one registered incoming edge from dandy-walker-syndrome, but NO EDGE IS REGISTERED HERE between them. The located evidence in this batch addresses spinal deformity, renal decline and mood and does not quantify hydrocephalus in this population, so the most clinically obvious neighbour is deliberately left unmapped rather than mapped on inference.

TWO ANCHORS DO NOT CONVERGE AND THIS IS STATED RATHER THAN PRESENTED AS CORROBORATION: the scoliosis cohort selected adults with spina bifida and found deformity at 53 percent, while the second scoliosis anchor selected children with congenital deformity and found occult dysraphism on MRI in 53.7 percent. The two similar figures describe opposite directions of the same relationship, which is the specific reason the second anchor is registered at all.

A NULL CARRIED INSIDE AN EDGE: the same cohort reported that 69 percent had chronic back pain with NO significant difference between those with and without scoliosis, recorded on the edge so the deformity cannot be used to explain pain in this population.
